analysis:
The only change in SSDPrefixCache.swift is a comment rewrite at lines 1081-1083 (head). The comment now says the sidecar write-ordering matters only when the whole donation does not fit the daily endurance bucket. The patch touches no executable code, so I found no change to behavior, crypto, tag derivation, TTL, salt scoping, staging reservations, or disk/budget guards.

I also read the surrounding head source in both units for T-041 context, without identifying anything new. Salt scoping is still folded into the chain hash and the HMAC tag (lines 533-542, 862-921). Lookup and endAdoption still match tickets exactly and pin per request (lines 548-575, 631-648). Donation is still gated by adoptionBound plus minEffectiveTokens (lines 883-888) and by the persisted-run byte cap (lines 938-947). The write-behind pre-check, the sidecar ordering after blocks (line 1087), and in-flight tag release on failure (lines 1013-1026, 1117-1125, 1243-1247) are unchanged. These are pre-existing and consistent with the T-041 mitigations.

I verified that the reworded comment matches the code: sidecars are appended after blocks at line 1087, and the pre-check at lines 1172-1177 is advisory, with the consumer's tryConsume remaining the authority. I did not see the SSDWriteBehind.consume implementation, so the claim about per-entry ordering in the comment is unverified, but it has no security impact since only comments changed. No new attack surface or threat-model gap.
